articles.title: JWST and ALMA reveal a dusty, rapidly growing black hole in the early universe
articles.description: A new study reveals a dust-reddened quasar from a time when the universe was less than a billion years old. Located at a redshift of 6.5488, the object J1440+0019 contains a rapidly accreting supermassive black hole with a mass of about 1.1 billion suns. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 9.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST and ALMA telescopes have jointly revealed a rapidly growing dust-shrouded black hole from when the universe was less than a billion years old. This landmark discovery challenges theories about how supermassive black holes formed so quickly.

articles.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
articles.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.
articles.summary: Smithsonian scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe, mapping the first 2 billion years of cosmic evolution. This breakthrough provides unprecedented insights into the universe's formative period.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes within a single galaxy from over 12.5 billion light-years away, dating to the dawn of time. This remarkable find challenges existing models of black hole formation in the early universe.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of what may be the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. This historic discovery opens an entirely new frontier in exoplanet science.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu mission reveal 4.5-billion-year-old secrets about our Solar System's formation. This landmark discovery is rewriting scientific understanding of planetary origins.

articles.title: Nasa beschleunigt Mondpläne: Landung 2028, Mondbasis ab Jahresende
articles.description: Die Nasa hält an einer bemannten Mondlandung im Jahr 2028 fest und ändert dafür die Architektur des Artemis-Programms. Ein Überblick.
articles.summary: NASA accelerates its lunar exploration plans, targeting a crewed moon landing in 2028 and establishing a lunar base by year-end through an updated Artemis program architecture. This represents a major milestone in humanity's return to the Moon.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Offers Clues to Protect Crews From Mars Dust
articles.description: Over 1,645 Martian days, NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover measured the fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles found clinging to samples of spacesuit materials that are carried aboard the rover, including some that are small enough to penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream. The findings will be published Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the Proceedings of […]
articles.summary: Over nearly 4.5 years on Mars, NASA's Perseverance rover has gathered critical data on Martian dust composition and behavior, essential for protecting future human crews on the Red Planet.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully lifts off to explore Phobos, marking an ambitious international step in understanding Mars's intriguing moons.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: The BepiColombo mission celebrates a major milestone as it continues its remarkable journey to Mercury, marking eight years of groundbreaking solar system exploration.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope makes its first discovery of a previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional capability for solar system observations.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA's Solar Orbiter spacecraft directly observes and helps explain mysterious S-shaped 'switchbacks' in the solar magnetic field, advancing our understanding of the Sun's behavior.

articles.title: Hubble Will Give the Roman Space Telescope a Helping Hand
articles.description: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will use gravitational microlensing to study dark matter. But it's a wide-field survey telescope, and the venerable Hubble Space Telescope can do things it can't do. That's why the Hubble is lending a hand.
articles.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will partner with Hubble to use gravitational microlensing to study dark matter in unprecedented detail.

articles.title: A Huge and Powerful New Simulation Helps Explain the Universe's Reionization
articles.description: Cosmologists have another powerful simulation to work with. Lumina is the one of the largest and most detailed cosmological simulations yet and runs on the Frontier supercomputer. It's larger and more detailed than Illustris TNG.
articles.summary: The powerful Lumina simulation becomes one of the largest and most detailed tools for understanding the universe's reionization period.

articles.title: Parker Solar Probe Spots Twisted Magnetic Braids Growing in the Solar Wind
articles.description: The magnetic environment around the Sun is a jumbled mess of chaotic fields and streams of charged particles. Recently we’ve been getting at least slightly better at mapping out its complexity, thanks in large part to data collected by missions like the Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter. But there’s still a large grey area surrounding the interface between the large scale hydrodynamic properties of plasmas and the microscopic properties of individual ions, and scientists believe understanding large scale features of the Sun, such as why its corona is so much hotter than its surface, may rely on our knowledge of that interface. A new paper that directly tackles some of the outstanding questions about that interface was recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters by Masatomi Iizawa of the Technical University of Braunschweig and his co-authors.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe discovers twisted magnetic braids forming in the solar wind, revealing new details about the Sun's magnetic environment.

articles.title: Webb links interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS to worlds beyond Neptune through similar ice signatures
articles.description: A Southwest Research Institute–led study used NASA's James Webb Space Telescope to examine ice grains streaming from interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, just the third object from beyond our solar system ever identified. The observations point to tiny aggregates of water ice and dust, about a micron or smaller.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope data links interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS to distant worlds beyond Neptune through matching ice composition signatures.

articles.title: Stellar collisions may have been common when the universe was young
articles.description: In our solar system's corner of the galaxy, stars rarely collide. It makes sense: Space is vast, and stars have room to roam. Even in most of the present-day universe, stellar collisions are rare. The James Webb Space Telescope, however, peers deep enough into space to see the universe as it was not too long after the Big Bang. Its observations have revealed extraordinarily compact stellar systems, raising the possibility that collisions between stars were once much more common.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New research suggests stellar collisions were far more common in the early universe than in our current cosmic neighborhood. This discovery reshapes our understanding of how stars interacted during the universe's youth.

articles.title: James Webb discovers a scorching lava planet with a “giant sunscreen”
articles.description: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away has surprised astronomers by apparently maintaining a thick atmosphere despite conditions that should have stripped it away billions of years ago. James Webb Space Telescope observations suggest that TOI-561 b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, possibly because of mineral clouds that act like a giant sunscreen. The planet may also be continually replenishing its atmosphere through gases released from a global ocean of molten rock.
articles.summary: James Webb discovered a scorching lava planet 280 light-years away that mysteriously maintains a thick atmosphere despite extreme surface temperatures. This surprising finding opens new questions about planetary atmospheres in extreme environments.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Using a balloon-borne telescope, astronomers have uncovered a surprisingly complex magnetic web above the Sun's surface. This discovery reveals hidden complexity in solar physics.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars provides new evidence about dark energy and the universe's expansion. This comprehensive study advances our understanding of cosmic acceleration.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 27, 1961: NASA launches Saturn I rocket on 1st test flight from Florida to set stage for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket
articles.description: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On October 27, 1961, NASA successfully launched the Saturn I rocket on its first test flight, paving the way for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket. This historic milestone marked a critical step toward lunar exploration.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.description: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On October 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft captured the first close-up images of Saturn's moon Titan, a landmark achievement in planetary exploration. These historic photographs revealed unprecedented details of this fascinating icy moon.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Scientists explore the Giant Impact Hypothesis, proposing that a planet-sized object collided with ancient Earth to create the moon. This theory provides fascinating insights into the dramatic origins of our lunar companion.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL celebrates 90 years of innovation while envisioning ambitious future missions including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters. The institution demonstrates remarkable commitment to expanding humanity's reach across the solar system and beyond.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers confirm the first microblazar discovery, a compact cosmic object with properties distinct from larger blazars. This finding expands our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena in the universe.

articles.title: How a Johnson Mentor Shapes the Next Generation of NASA Talent
articles.description: When Rice University student Malvika Bhardwaj asked her mentor Daniel Cohen, a Guidance, Navigation & Control (GN&C) engineer at NASA’s Johnson Space Center, whether he had time to keep teaching interns with his busy workload, he answered, “You decide what’s important.”  In honor of National Mentoring Day on Oct. 27, Bhardwaj reflects on how Cohen’s […]
articles.summary: A Rice University student working with a NASA Johnson Space Center mentor in Guidance, Navigation & Control engineering represents the inspiring pipeline of talent entering the space industry.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Views Dust at Neretva Vallis
articles.description: Description This 360-degree look at Neretva Vallis within Mars’ Jezero Crater was stitched together using 217 images acquired by the rover’s Mastcam-Z on May 20, 2024, the 1,155th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. While it is a wind-swept dusty vista today, billions of years ago it was home to a river channel that fed fresh water into […]
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover captures a 360-degree panoramic view of Neretva Vallis in Mars's Jezero Crater using 217 stitched images, revealing the geological features of an ancient river delta.

articles.title: NASA SEES Interns Tackle Real-World Challenges in Lunar Exploration
articles.description: The NASA STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) Enhancement in Earth Science (SEES) Internship Program at the University of Texas Center for Space Research places high school students on small, mission-focused research teams mentored by NASA, academic, and industry experts. During summer 2026, the SEES Mission Architecture Tool for Research, Integration, and eXploration (MATRIX) team […]
articles.summary: NASA's SEES Internship Program engages STEM students in tackling real-world challenges in lunar exploration, inspiring the next generation of space scientists and engineers.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: A stunning image captures the stellar nursery within a nebula where new stars are actively forming, showcasing the cosmic process of star birth.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission prepares for launch aboard an H3 rocket, embarking on an exciting mission to study Mars's enigmatic moons.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: European Space Agency's Mars Express reveals new insights into an unusual Martian cloud formation using advanced meteorological modeling.
